## Verdict

wrong

## Bearer

HyresultResultParser — core-domain/src/main/kotlin/com/mgilli/core/domain/race/HyresultResultParser.kt

## Trigger

`PasteResultViewModel.onImportClicked` calling `HyresultResultParser.parse(pastedText)` — observed

## Today

`parse` skips at most one leading row, and only when that row's fourth
column (`firstColumns[3]`) fails `parseTimeValue` — a check built and
tested against a captured layout of exactly four columns per row:
rank, label, diff, cumulative (`valid_result_with_header.txt`,
`HyresultResultParserTest`, `CURRENT_TECHNICAL_STATE.md` line 661-662).
Every data row is then read on that fixed assumption: `columns[1]` is
taken as the label, `columns[2]` as the segment's own diff, `columns[3]`
as the cumulative time — there is no column for a "Time of Day" value
anywhere in the file, and no grep for `Time of Day` / `TimeOfDay` /
`timeOfDay` returns a hit inside `HyresultResultParser.kt`. Nothing in
the file, or anywhere in `core-domain`, mentions a trailing total row:
a grep for `Total`, case-insensitive, returns no match in
`core-domain`. Once the fixed 30 data rows are consumed, any further
row — including a closing `Total time` row — is read as segment 31
and either fails `INSUFFICIENT_COLUMNS`/`INVALID_TIME_VALUE`/
`UNKNOWN_LABEL` on that row, or is accepted as data and pushes the
count to `TOO_MANY_SEGMENTS`. `parseTimeValue` itself already parses
both `m:ss` and `h:mm:ss` generically (`components.size !in 2..3`
guards, `HyresultResultParserTest`'s dedicated test for a 3-component
cumulative value at rank 27 passes today) — an hour-crossing duration
is not rejected for its component count by this function.

## Expected

`parse` recognises and skips the real Hyresult export's leading header
row — `Split`, `Time of Day`, `Time`, `Diff` — and its closing
`Total time` row, neither of which names a split, without shifting any
data row's position in the 30-segment cycle. Each data row's diff and
cumulative values are read from the columns the real export actually
carries them in, `Time of Day` included, whatever its position among
the columns is — not from a fixed index that assumes no such column
exists. A cumulative or diff value past the hour, written with three
components (`1:01:40`), is read the same way as one written with two.
